Report of Finding and Sanction 
Emma Elizabeth SMITH  2024/1532/D5 
The Bar Tribunals and Adjudication Service 
 
Page 2 of 6 
1. In accordance with an appointment made by the President of the Council of the Inns 
of Court contained in a Convening Order dated 18 March 2026, The Tribunal sat on 8 
April 2026 to hear and determine 3 charges of professional misconduct contrary to 
the Code of Conduct of the Bar of England and Wales against Emma Elizabeth Smith 
barrister of the Honourable Society of Lincoln's Inn. 
Charges 
2. The following charges were admitted 
Charge 1  
Statement of Offence  
Professional misconduct, contrary to Core Duty 3 and/or rC8 of the Bar Standards 
Board Handbook (version 4.8).  
Particulars of Offence  
Emma Smith, a barrister, failed to act with honesty and with integrity and/or acted in a 
way which could reasonably be seen by the public to undermine her honesty and 
integrity, in that, on 19 June 2024, at a hearing in the Family Court, she advanced an 
application for an order to change the nursery of her client’s child, which application 
gave the impression that the child was yet to move to an alternative nursery. This 
was misleading, as her client had already moved the child to an alternative nursery, 
in breach of an existing Specific Issue Order. Ms Smith knew this, as her client had 
told her in a conference on 5 June 2024. Ms Smith failed to draw this relevant fact to 
the Court’s attention. 
 
Charge 2  
Statement of Offence  
Professional misconduct, contrary to Core Duty 1 of the Bar Standards Board 
Handbook (version 4.8). 
Particulars of Offence  
Emma Smith, a barrister, failed to observe her duty to the court in the administration 
of justice, in that, on 19 June 2024, at a hearing in the Family Court, she advanced 
an application for an order to change the nursery of her client’s child, which 
application gave the impression that the child was yet to move to an alternative 
nursery. This was misleading, as her client had already moved the child to an

Emma Elizabeth SMITH  2024/1532/D5 
The Bar Tribunals and Adjudication Service 
 
Page 3 of 6 
alternative nursery, in breach of an existing Specific Issue Order. Ms Smith knew this, 
as her client had told her in a conference on 5 June 2024. Ms Smith failed to draw 
this relevant fact to the Court’s attention. 
 
Charge 3  
Statement of Offence  
Professional misconduct, contrary to rC6.1a of the Bar Standards Board Handbook 
(version 4.8).  
Particulars of Offence  
Emma Smith, a barrister, made submissions, representations or a statement which 
she knew or was instructed were untrue or misleading, in that, on 19 June 2024, at a 
hearing in the Family Court, she told the Court that her client had made an 
application to move her child to an alternative nursery, thereby giving the impression 
that the child was yet to move to the alternative nursery. This was misleading, as her 
client had already moved the child to an alternative nursery, in breach of an existing 
Specific Issue Order. Ms Smith knew this, as her client had told her in a conference 
on 5 June 2024. Ms Smith failed to draw this relevant fact to the Court’s attention 
 
Parties Present and Representation 
3. The Respondent was present and was not represented. The Bar Standards Board 
(“BSB”) was represented by Winston Jacob. 
Findings and Sanction 
4. Emma Smith was called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn on the 13th of October 2005. She 
entered practice on the western circuit and., with a career break, continued in 
practice on that circuit until recently. 
5. She faces charges of dishonesty in respect of her conduct at a family hearing before 
DJ Murray on the 19th of June 2024. She has admitted those charges and, to her 
credit, has never sought to evade responsibility for what she did. 
6. The background to that hearing is a matrimonial dispute relating to a three year-old 
child. 

Report of Finding and Sanction 
Emma Elizabeth SMITH  2024/1532/D5 
The Bar Tribunals and Adjudication Service 
 
Page 4 of 6 
7. On the 22nd of December 2023 the Family Court made a Specific Issues Order 
requiring that child to attend a specific nursery until and unless a different order was 
made. Ms Smith was not instructed in the case when that order was made. 
8. She was, however, instructed by early June because on the 5th of June 2024 she 
had a conference with the mother of the child who was by then her lay client. In that 
conference Miss Smith was told that because of difficulties with the father who was 
harassing her at the nursery, which was near where he worked, she, the mother, had 
moved the child out of that nursery and into another nursery without seeking 
permission from the Court. 
9. Ms Smith advised her that she was in breach of the order and that she needed to 
make a retrospective application to the Court to permit the move that had already 
taken place and regularise the situation. That was obviously the correct advice to 
give. 
10. On the 10th of May 2024 a written application was made seeking permission to 
change nursery. It was implicit in that application that the child had not actually 
moved, whereas the true position was of course different. Miss Smith was not 
responsible for the drafting of that application. 
11. The application came on before DJ Murray on the 19th of June 2024.It was opposed. 
The father, who was appearing in person, was present of the hearing, as was Ms 
Smith representing the mother. DJ Murray did not know that the move to the new 
nursery had actually taken place and neither did the father, and Miss Smith never 
told either of them during the course of the hearing that the move of nursery had 
actually taken place even though she knew that it had. 
12. We have a transcript of the hearing that took place. It is obvious from that transcript 
that Miss Smith allowed the father and DJ Murray to be misled about what the true 
situation was. 
13. It is perhaps sufficient that two examples illustrating DJ Murray’s state of mind can be 
particularised. 
14. At page B 26 there is a passage which shows that the district judge and father 
thought that the child was still at the original nursery because a query was raised as 
to whether there was a place for the child to go to. In fact, as Ms Smith knew, there 
was and the child had already gone. She should have intervened to explain that that 
had happened, but she did not. 

Report of Finding and Sanction 
Emma Elizabeth SMITH  2024/1532/D5 
The Bar Tribunals and Adjudication Service 
 
Page 5 of 6 
15. At page B 41 DJ Murray said “it's very tempting to try to resolve the nursery issue 
now but I think if we do that, it's going to be a half cocked attempt” Here there was an 
obvious positive duty on Ms Smith to intervene but she did not and instead allowed 
the district judge and the father to be misled 
16. The father, it should be pointed out, expressed opposition to any move of nursery 
taking place so it was of particular importance that he should be aware of what the 
mother had done. 
17. The hearing was adjourned. Two hours later, Miss Smith having considered her 
conduct at the hearing, reported herself to the BSB. 
18. She accepts, as she has accepted throughout, that she deliberately allowed the 
Court to be misled about what the true nursery position was. The phrase that she 
adopted was that she had allowed her clients interest to take precedence over her 
duty to the Court. She accepts, and in our judgement rightly accepts, that her 
behaviour in allowing the Court to be misled on a matter that was in dispute between 
the parties and in particular where the opposing party was not represented amounted 
to professional dishonesty.  
19. She does not seek to excuse herself nor does she ask for any other sanction than 
disbarment. We commend her frankness before this tribunal. 
20. She has now left practice at the bar and is pursuing another career. She has no wish 
to return to the bar even though in a powerful reference her former head of chambers 
indicated that she would be welcome to return if only she wanted to. 
21. We have to consider, whatever her view, the appropriate sanction in what is a case 
of admitted dishonesty. Here what is of paramount importance is maintaining the 
confidence of the public in the integrity of the profession and its practitioners. 
Dishonesty, particularly in the face of the court, strikes at the heart of that confidence. 
For that reason even where, as here, there were no serious long term consequences, 
because the move to the new nursery was later allowed, the only sanction, unless 
there are exceptional circumstances is disbarment. 
22.  We do not know why she chose to act in a way that we accept was completely out of 
character for an otherwise exemplary practitioner and nor, we think does she, but 
that cannot amount to an exceptional circumstance. 
23. There are in truth no other exceptional circumstances that we are invited to find or 
can find. 

Report of Finding and Sanction 
Emma Elizabeth SMITH  2024/1532/D5 
The Bar Tribunals and Adjudication Service 
 
Page 6 of 6 
24. Accordingly, our order is that Ms Smith be disbarred. 
25. An order for the BSB not to issue a practicing certificate pending any appeal is also 
made. 
26. The Treasurer of the Honourable Society of Lincoln's Inn is requested to take action 
on this report in accordance with rE239 of the Disciplinary Tribunal Regulations 2017  
Costs 
27. The Tribunal ordered costs of £3,210 payable to the BSB within three months of the 
hearing date. 
 
 
Dated: 5 May 2026 
HH Nicholas Ainley 
Chairman of the Tribunal

summary: On 8 April 2026 the Tribunal disbarred Ms Smith and imposed an immediate suspension pending any appeal. Costs: £3,210 payable to the BSB Full reasons to follow
